patch_description:
This version replaces the high-variance innovation-only tracker with a robust endpoint-regression measurement model combined with a conservative alpha-beta trend tracker.

For every sliding window, it computes an exponentially recency-weighted local linear regression evaluated at the newest sample. This provides a low-lag, endpoint-aligned estimate rather than the delayed estimate of a moving average. A second Huber-weighted regression pass reduces the influence of spikes and transient outliers.

The endpoint estimate is then fused with a predictive level/slope state. Measurement gain increases only for sustained, significant movement and is capped to avoid noise chasing. Trend-direction hysteresis and slope deadband suppress small noise-induced sign changes while allowing genuine reversals to be confirmed quickly. The result retains endpoint responsiveness while reducing false reversals and unnecessary slope changes.
